assertions.text: Table has at least one column name ending with '?' (e.g. 'Discount?' or 'Expected?')
Table has exactly 3 data rows (GOLD, SILVER, BRONZE)
assertions.evidence: Gold customer | GOLD | 20; Silver customer | SILVER | 10; Bronze customer | BRONZE | 0

assertions.text: Test method body contains only one assertEquals (or equivalent assertion) — not three
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method body contains only a single assertEquals; no control flow

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: Scenario | Customer tier | Discount? (Scenario is leftmost)

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case
If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as fixed values shared by all rows, where/when the rule applies, or open questions
assertions.evidence: @Description("Order value is 100 for all scenarios.") conveys fixed input

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order
If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description text is single short line; textblock requirement N/A
